name: s1-retrofit
notes: Suite S1 complete (24 Oct 2026): all ten features and the change request have specifications, visible tests, hidden tests and a cumulative reference solution (reference/source.py, built with reference/build_reference.py). Have the hidden tests reviewed against the rules, then freeze the suite.

features.title: Homes and retrofit cases
features.story: As a programme officer, I want to register homes and open retrofit cases so that I can see all the work in one list.
rules: A home has a UPRN (a non-empty string of digits, unique), an address (required) and a postcode (required; stored trimmed and upper-case).
A case belongs to one home and one measure: loft insulation, cavity wall insulation, external wall insulation, air source heat pump, solar pv or windows.
A home cannot have two cases for the same measure.
Case ids are C-0001, C-0002, ... in creation order.
list_cases returns cases ordered by id, optionally filtered by postcode prefix (case-insensitive) and by measure.
CSV import (header uprn,address,postcode) is all-or-nothing: if any row is invalid or duplicated, within the file or against existing homes, nothing is imported.
api: add_home(uprn, address, postcode) -> Home with attributes uprn, address, postcode.
open_case(uprn, measure) -> Case with attributes id, uprn, measure.
ValidationError for invalid input and NotFoundError for unknown homes or cases, both importable from workbench.

features.title: Case lifecycle
features.story: As a programme officer, I want each case to move through the retrofit lifecycle so that I know where every case stands.
rules: Stages, in order: candidate, surveyed, designed, ready, installed, handed_over. New cases start as candidate.

A case moves forward exactly one stage at a time. Skipping a stage, staying in the same stage or moving backwards raises InvalidTransition, a subclass of ValidationError. An unknown stage raises ValidationError.
Every move names who made it (by, a non-empty string) and is recorded in the case history as (from_stage, to_stage, by), oldest first. A failed move changes nothing.
list_cases can also filter by stage; stage_counts returns every stage with its number of cases, including zeros.
api: move(case_id, to, by) -> Case; Case gains the attribute stage.
history(case_id) -> list of (from_stage, to_stage, by) tuples.
stage_counts() -> dict from stage to count.

features.title: Ownership and handoffs
features.story: As a delivery lead, I want to hand cases between owners so that responsibility is always explicit.
rules: Every case has at most one owner. New cases have no owner (owner is None).
assign sets the first owner of an unowned case. Assigning a case that already has an owner raises NotAllowed (use a handoff instead).
Only the current owner may request a handoff (NotAllowed otherwise, including for unowned cases). The owner changes only when the recipient accepts; the recipient may instead decline with a reason.
Only the recipient may accept or decline (NotAllowed otherwise). Accepting or declining when no handoff is pending raises ValidationError.

A case has at most one pending handoff: requesting another while one is pending raises ValidationError, and so does a handoff to the current owner. Cases in stage handed_over cannot be handed off (NotAllowed).
owner, to, by and reason must be non-blank strings (ValidationError). Handoffs do not appear in the stage history.
list_cases can also filter by owner, combined with the other filters.
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.
api: pending_handoff(case_id) -> the pending recipient's name, or None
NotAllowed, a subclass of ValidationError, importable from workbench.

features.title: Returns and reopening
features.story: As a surveyor, I want to send a case back to an earlier stage with a reason, and to reopen a handed-over case, so that rework is visible.
rules: return_to moves a case back to any earlier stage, skipping stages if needed. A target that is not earlier than the current stage raises InvalidTransition; an unknown stage raises ValidationError.
reopen moves a handed_over case back to installed; reopening any other case raises InvalidTransition.
reason and by must be non-blank (ValidationError).
Returns and reopenings are recorded in the stage history like moves, as (from_stage, to_stage, by). Afterwards the case moves forward again one stage at a time.
notes(case_id) lists the reasons given for returns and reopenings, oldest first ([] if none).
Returning or reopening a case cancels its pending handoff, if any. The owner does not change.
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.

features.title: Safety holds
features.story: As a building-safety officer, I want to put a case on hold so that no work proceeds while a hazard is unresolved.
rules: place_hold puts a case on hold with a reason. Placing a hold on a case that is already on hold raises ValidationError. reason and by must be non-blank.
While a case is on hold, every move raises OnHold (a subclass of ValidationError), whatever the target stage, and handoffs cannot be requested or accepted (OnHold).
Returns, reopening and declining a pending handoff are still allowed while a case is on hold; the case stays on hold.
Only the role building_safety may release a hold (NotAllowed otherwise, and the hold stays). Releasing a case that is not on hold raises ValidationError.
holds(case_id) lists every hold, oldest first, as (placed_by, reason, released_by) tuples; released_by is None while the hold is active.
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.

features.title: Resident consent
features.story: As a resident liaison officer, I want to track resident consent so that nothing is installed without it where it is needed.
rules: Case.consent is one of not_required (the default for new cases), required, given or withdrawn. Cases whose consent is not_required behave exactly as before.
require_consent marks consent as required; calling it when consent is not not_required raises ValidationError.
record_consent sets consent to given from any other state; recording it when it is already given raises ValidationError.
A forward move into installed while consent is required raises ConsentRequired (a subclass of ValidationError). Other moves are not affected.

withdraw_consent works only when consent is given (ValidationError otherwise). It sets consent to withdrawn and pauses the case: Case.paused becomes True and every move raises Paused (a subclass of ValidationError) until consent is recorded again, which clears the pause. If the case is also on hold, OnHold is raised instead.
Returns, reopening and handoffs are still allowed while a case is paused.
by and reason must be non-blank (ValidationError).
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.
api: Case gains the attributes consent (str) and paused (bool).
ConsentRequired and Paused importable from workbench.

features.title: Appointments and no-access visits
features.story: As a scheduler, I want to track offered and confirmed appointments and failed visits so that stuck cases are escalated.
rules: Dates are datetime.date objects; anything else raises ValidationError. by must be non-blank.

offer_appointment offers a date; offering a date already offered for that case raises ValidationError. confirm_appointment confirms an offered date; confirming a date that is not currently offered (never offered, or already confirmed) raises ValidationError.
appointments(case_id) lists (date, status) tuples sorted by date; status is offered or confirmed.
While a case is on hold, offering or confirming appointments raises OnHold. No-access visits can still be recorded.

record_no_access records a visit where no access was gained; verified must be True or False (ValidationError otherwise). Only verified visits count: no_access_count is the number of verified visits in the active period, and a case with more than five is escalated.
escalated_cases() returns the escalated cases ordered by id.
Reopening a case starts a new active period: its no-access count goes back to 0, but no_access_history keeps every visit. Returns do not reset the count.
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.
api: no_access_history(case_id) -> list of (date, verified), in the order recorded

features.title: Roles and field visibility
features.story: As a data protection lead, I want contractors never to see residents' vulnerability reasons or contact details.
rules: set_vulnerability records why a resident is vulnerable; set_resident_contact records a resident's phone number. Both need a non-blank value (ValidationError) and a known UPRN (NotFoundError). Homes start with neither (None).

get_home(uprn) returns a Home with uprn, address, postcode, vulnerability and contact (NotFoundError for an unknown UPRN). case_details(case_id) returns a dict with exactly the keys id, uprn, address, postcode, measure, stage, owner, vulnerability and contact.
Roles are officer, contractor, building_safety and manager; any other role raises ValidationError. The Workbench itself sees everything, as do views for every role except contractor.

view_as(role) returns a read-only view with the read methods get_home, get_case, list_cases (same filters), case_details, history, notes and stage_counts, always reflecting the current state. Any other method on a view raises NotAllowed.

Contractors never see vulnerability reasons or resident contacts: in a contractor view, get_home and case_details return None for vulnerability and contact, and all other fields are unchanged. Viewing never changes the stored data.
Unknown case ids raise NotFoundError.
api: get_home(uprn) -> Home (Home gains vulnerability and contact)

features.title: Deterministic priority ranking
features.story: As a programme manager, I want a ranked list of cases with reasons so that crews work on the right homes first.
rules: rank_cases(policy_version='v1') ranks every case except those in stage handed_over and returns a list of (case_id, score, reason_codes) tuples, reason_codes being a list of strings. Any policy version other than 'v1' raises ValidationError.

Policy v1 points: VULNERABLE +50 when the home has a vulnerability recorded; ESCALATED +30 when the case is escalated; CONSENT_GIVEN +20 when consent is given; READY +10 when the stage is ready; PAUSED -40 when the case is paused. HELD (no points) when the case is on hold; held cases still collect the other codes and points.
reason_codes lists the codes that apply in this order: HELD, VULNERABLE, ESCALATED, CONSENT_GIVEN, READY, PAUSED.
Held cases come first; within each group, cases are ordered by score, highest first, and ties break by case id. The same state always gives the same ranking.
Views also offer rank_cases, with the same result.
api: rank_cases(policy_version='v1') -> list of (case_id, score, reason_codes), on the Workbench and on views

features.title: Audit trail and export
features.story: As an auditor, I want a tamper-evident record of every change and a filtered export of cases.
rules: Every successful write appends exactly one entry to the audit trail; failed calls and reads append nothing. The writes are add_home (an import appends one add_home entry per home), open_case, move, assign, request_handoff, accept_handoff, decline_handoff, return_to, reopen, place_hold, release_hold, require_consent, record_consent, withdraw_consent, offer_appointment, confirm_appointment, record_no_access, set_vulnerability and set_resident_contact.

Each entry is a dict with exactly the keys seq (1, 2, 3, ...), action (the method name), target (the case id, or the UPRN for home methods), by (the by argument, or None for methods without one), prev_hash (the previous entry's hash, or '' for the first) and hash (a 64-character SHA-256 hex digest covering seq, action, target, by and prev_hash).

The hash input is the UTF-8 encoding of json.dumps([seq, action, target, by, prev_hash], ensure_ascii=True, separators=(', ', ': ')), with the entry's values in that order and no trailing newline. This public canonical JSON encoding uses null for None, ASCII escapes for non-ASCII characters, and one space after each comma. Compute the lowercase SHA-256 hex digest of those exact bytes.

audit_log() returns copies of the entries, oldest first. verify_audit(entries=None) checks the given list of entries (the workbench's own trail when None): it returns True only if every entry's seq is its position (1, 2, 3, ...), every prev_hash equals the previous entry's hash and every hash matches the entry's content.

export_cases_csv(role, **filters) returns CSV text with the header id,uprn,address,postcode,measure,stage,owner,vulnerability,contact and one row per case returned by list_cases(**filters), in the same order. Missing values (such as no owner) are empty fields. For contractors, vulnerability and contact are always empty. An unknown role raises ValidationError.

change_request.title: Regions
change_request.story: As the programme director, I want every home to belong to a region and every user to work only within their regions.
rules: define_region(name, postcode_prefixes) defines a region by one or more postcode prefixes, stored upper-case. A blank name, a name already defined, the name 'unassigned', an empty prefix list, a blank prefix or a prefix already used by any region raises ValidationError.

Every home belongs to exactly one region: region_of(uprn) returns the region whose prefix is the longest match for the home's postcode, or 'unassigned' if none matches. Regions apply to homes added before or after they are defined. Unknown UPRNs raise NotFoundError.

add_user(name, role, regions) registers a user with one of the roles officer, contractor, building_safety or manager and one or more defined regions. A blank or existing name, an unknown role, an empty region list or an undefined region raises ValidationError.

view_for(name) returns a read-only view for a registered user (NotFoundError otherwise): the same view as view_as(role) for the user's role, plus rank_cases and export_cases_csv(**filters), restricted to homes in the user's regions. Lists, rankings, exports and stage counts include only those cases, in the same order as before; reading a case or home outside them raises NotAllowed.

A handoff to a registered user whose regions do not include the case's region needs a manager's approval: accept_handoff raises NotAllowed until approve_handoff is called by a registered user with role manager (NotAllowed for anyone else). handoff_needs_approval(case_id) says whether the pending handoff still needs approval. Approving when no pending handoff needs approval raises ValidationError. Each new request needs its own approval. Handoffs to anyone else work as before.
define_region, add_user and approve_handoff are writes and are audited like the others (target: the region name, the user name or the case id; by: None, None and the approver).
Everything that worked before keeps working.
